No, dreaming does not only take place during REM sleep. According to the NIH, "most of your dreaming occurs during REM sleep, although some can also occur in non-REM sleep" [d1]. The Sleep Foundation explicitly calls the idea that REM is the only stage where dreams occur "a common myth about sleep," noting that REM dreams tend to be more vivid than non-REM dreams [d2]. The American Academy of Family Physicians states even more directly that "dreaming occurs in all stages of sleep," with 80% of people reporting dreams when woken from REM or sleep-onset stages and 40% reporting dreams when woken from deep sleep [d6]. Research from Aalto University and the University of Wisconsin found that subjects woken from NREM sleep reported dreams in more than half of cases, with longer dream reports correlating with brain activity resembling wakefulness [d3]. Healthline similarly confirms that "dreams can happen during any stage of sleep, but the vivid ones that you remember tend to happen during REM sleep" [d4].
